# Tool Selection Guide

> Generated from [`internal/mcpcatalog/tools.go`](../internal/mcpcatalog/tools.go),
> [`internal/mcp/toolsurface/toolsurface.go`](../internal/mcp/toolsurface/toolsurface.go), and
> [`internal/mcp/toolpolicy.go`](../internal/mcp/toolpolicy.go).
> If this guide and those files disagree, those files win.

kern ships a **32-tool** MCP catalog and advertises the **full catalog by default** (standing mandate 2026-10-23: agents use all available tools). Every tool is advertised on `tools/list`; `kern_meta` routes natural language to any of them.

## Surface

| Mode | Tools |
|---|---:|
| Default | 32 |
| Full (`KERN_MCP_FULL=1`) | 32 |
| Router-only (`KERN_MCP_SINGLE_TOOL=1`) | 1 |
| High-level (`KERN_MCP_HIGH_LEVEL_ONLY=1`) | 6 |
| Phase filter (`KERN_MCP_PHASE`) | Default/full subset plus `meta` and `cross` tools |
| Category filter (`KERN_MCP_CATEGORY`) | One category plus `kern_meta` |
| Allowlist (`KERN_TOOLS`) | Execution gate applied on every call |

The default surface is:

`kern_meta`, `kern_explore`, `kern_impact`, `kern_apply`, `kern_search`, `kern_verify`, `kern_buddy`, `kern_exec`, `kern_compact_file`, `kern_run`, `kern_optimize`, `kern_context`, `kern_memory`, `kern_evidence`, `kern_probe`, `kern_plan`, `kern_doc`, `kern_project_map`, `kern_ast_search`, `kern_stats`, `kern_why`, `kern_heal`, `kern_fit_context`, `kern_plan_context`, `kern_path`, `kern_semcache`, `kern_swap`, `kern_mask_pii`, `kern_fetch_raw_anchor`, `kern_review`, `kern_graph`, `kern_arch`.

`kern_exec` is advertised for discoverability only. Every execution attempt still fails closed unless explicitly enabled through `KERN_ALLOW_EXEC` or an allowlist policy.

## Choose by intent

| Intent | Best tool | Why |
|---|---|---|
| New repo or unfamiliar project | `kern_buddy` | Onboarding digest, layout, conventions, memory |
| Find a symbol by name | `kern_search` | Ranked symbol lookup |
| Structural pattern (`func greet`, `type *User*`) | `kern_ast_search` | AST-aware search |
| Understand one symbol deeply | `kern_explore` | Definition, callers, callees, blast radius |
| Need only the exact source slice | `kern_context` | Minimal definition and direct edges |
| Understand a file's structure | `kern_compact_file` | Functions, types, line numbers; `tier=full` for verbatim |
| Explain why a symbol matters | `kern_why` | Rationale, docs, dependency counts |
| Plan a change | `kern_plan` | Deterministic affected files, risks, validation |
| Pre-select context for a change | `kern_plan_context` | Avoids over-fetching |
| Fit selected files/symbols in a token budget | `kern_fit_context` | Tiered AST folding |
| Assess blast radius | `kern_impact` | Change impact analysis |
| Review changed files | `kern_review` | Token-optimized review context |
| Run verification | `kern_verify` | Build/tests/security checks and command slices |
| Self-correct failing files | `kern_heal` | Validation loop in a throwaway snapshot |
| Whole-project map | `kern_project_map` | File/symbol map |
| Search project docs | `kern_doc` (`action=search`) | Local doc index |
| Remember or recall project lessons | `kern_memory` | Cross-session project memory |
| Compress a prompt, log, or output | `kern_optimize` | Token reduction and masking |
| Mask secrets/PII | `kern_mask_pii` | Local-only scan |
| Inspect semantic cache | `kern_semcache` | Stats/list/clear/similarity |
| Re-read truncated output | `kern_fetch_raw_anchor` | Full retained output slices |
| Find a call path | `kern_path` | Shortest in-project call route |
| Run a full intent pipeline | `kern_run` | Explore/plan/edit/verify orchestration |
| Produce signed evidence | `kern_evidence` | Verify/explain/export/anchor |
| Swap code blocks with symbolic signatures | `kern_swap` | Context compression |
| Unsure which tool to call | `kern_meta` | Natural-language router |

## Risk model

| Risk | Count | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| low | 20 | Read-only or locally contained operations |
| medium | 8 | Analysis, planning, memory, docs, verification |
| high | 3 | Orchestration and self-repair |
| critical | 1 | Governed command execution |

## Principles

1. Start with `kern_buddy` for onboarding or `kern_meta` when the intent is already known.
2. Prefer the narrowest useful tool: `kern_context` before `kern_explore`, and `kern_compact_file` before reading a whole file.
3. Use `kern_plan` or `kern_plan_context` before edits.
4. Use `kern_review` and `kern_verify` after edits.
5. Treat `kern_exec` as an explicitly governed capability, never as an ordinary fallback.
